title: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Incident Review
topics: Launch readiness checklist for next release
summary: Internal incident review focused on KV cache eviction that caused elevated latencies and increased cost for a subset of Dedicated pools. We validated root cause (regression in batching changes + kernel selection edge-case), agreed on short-term mitigations (patch, tighter autoscaler rules for a week, manual flush on affected hosts) and longer-term roadmap changes (better canarying, synthetic traffic for KV cache stress tests, telemetry additions). Next steps: engineering to push patch and schedule canary; SRE to update playbook; product to delay non-critical launch items until verification complete.
action_items: Dana Liu - produce RCA doc and timeline for fix deployment - due 2026-04-02
Omar Habib - backport kernel-selection patch and open PR for review - due 2026-04-01
Sam Rodriguez - run dedicated canary with synthetic KV-heavy traffic and report metrics - due 2026-04-06
Lena Ortiz - update launch checklist and notify release stakeholders of potential delay - due 2026-03-31
Marcus Yi - add synthetic KV cache stress tests to nightly CI - due 2026-04-09
next_steps: Share RCA draft with leadership and legal for compliance note
Schedule dry-run canary on dedicated pool (Tues 2026-04-06)
Patch deployment to staging then canary, monitor 48h before full rollout
Update runbook and pager thresholds for cache eviction events
transcript:
Meeting: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Incident Review
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 1:15
Attendees: Priya Nair, Sam Rodriguez, Dana Liu, Omar Habib, Lena Ortiz, Elena Park, Marcus Yi, Arjun Singh, Tanya Morales

Summary: quick internal postmortem for KV cache eviction incident on 2026-03-28 that affected Redwood Dedicated pools; discuss mitigations and launch readiness impacts.

Topics: Postmortem; fix and rollout plan; canary strategy; telemetry gaps; launch checklist adjustments.

--- Transcript (auto-generated, medium quality, some recognition errors) ---
0:00 Priya Nair: ok everyone, thanks for joining, let's get started. we're here to review the cache eviction incident from last Saturday and decide next steps for the upcoming release. i want to keep this to 60-ish minutes, we'll run over if needed.
0:18 Sam Rodriguez: yeah, i'll go over the timeline and metrics first, quick caveat i don't have the final logs from the on-call handoff, but the dashboard is up to date.
0:30 Sam Rodriguez: so at 03:12 UTC on 03-28 we observed a sudden spike in tail latency for a subset of Dedicated nodes, p50 p95 p99 all moved up, token throughput dropped, cost per token increased as batching collapsed, and we saw a correlated increase in kernel time for attention ops.
0:48 Dana Liu: just to add, we saw a bunch of cache evictions, the prefix/KV cache entries were being evicted unusually fast; memory pressure on those hosts spiked even though we hadn't changed instance sizes.
1:06 Omar Habib: right, and our initial hypothesis was autoscaler churn + unexpected kernel selection path that didn't use quantized kernels for long sequences. that combination yielded higher memory use and caused the eviction.
1:26 Elena Park: sorry, quick q, is this the same root cause as the Friday patch we rolled for batching? i thought the batching change was supposed to reduce memory use.
1:36 Sam Rodriguez: good point, the batching change optimizes request grouping, but in edge cases it created longer-lived batch windows for certain tail clients which increased concurrent KV cache entries. combined with the kernel selection regression, we hit a sweet spot for eviction.
1:52 Tanya Morales: does this affect only Dedicated or also Hosted?
1:58 Dana Liu: mainly Dedicated pools in eu-west-2 and us-west-1 where we had high conc bursts; hosted saw some elevated latencies but autoscaler there mitigated it faster.
2:12 Priya Nair: ok so timeline confirmed. who confirmed the kernel-selection regression?
2:20 Omar Habib: i dug in this morning — there was a fallback path introduced late last quarter that erroneously skipped a quantized kernel for certain attention shapes. it's rare, happens when seq len distributions are ... uh, in the mid-range and batching windows align oddly.
2:38 Marcus Yi: transcription note: kernel selection path -> kernel selection path regression (slight misrec)
2:44 Priya Nair: thanks. what's the immediate impact on launch readiness if we don't fix before canary?
2:52 Lena Ortiz: launch items dependent on Dedicated throughput need to be paused; non-critical UI/console changes can continue but we should freeze capacity-increasing features until the canary passes. i recommend we delay the big customer-facing rollout by one week to be safe.
3:12 Sam Rodriguez: operational mitigation we did: manual pod restarts on affected hosts, tightened autoscaler cooldown to reduce churn, and temporarily disabled the new batching window on the small cohort. that bought us time.
3:30 Dana Liu: yeah but that's brittle. we need a patch to kernel selection and a backfill to include better unit tests for the kernel paths. also we didn't have an alert specifically for abnormal KV eviction rate — we relied on latency alerts.
3:46 Omar Habib: agreed, i'm preparing a patch now to restore the correct selection logic and add a flag to force quantized kernel on suspicious shapes. it's in my local branch, i'll open a PR today.
3:58 Priya Nair: good. what's the plan for canary? sampling, metrics and rollback criteria?
4:06 Sam Rodriguez: plan: canary on one dedicated pool with synthetic KV-heavy traffic that mimics tail clients, monitor p50/p95/p99, kernel CPU time, eviction rate, memory usage. gates: if p99 improves and eviction rate normalizes and cost delta under 5% for 48h, we roll out. rollback if p99 > baseline by 10% or eviction rate > x. we'll refine numbers in the doc.
4:34 Elena Park: for stakeholders, can we provide a short note for sales/CS? they noticed customer jira tickets.
4:40 Lena Ortiz: i'll draft a communications note and post to #launch-notify; we should include mitigation steps and ETA.
4:46 Marcus Yi: QA needs a clear test plan — i'll add synthetic tests to nightly and run a stress test during the canary.
4:54 Priya Nair: thanks. telemetry gaps — where did we miss signals?
5:02 Dana Liu: two things: no eviction-rate specific alert, and our kernel-selection telemetry is coarse; we only log selection counts every 15m. we need more granular tracing for kernel path decisions and an alert on sudden spike in eviction rate per host.
5:20 Omar Habib: i can add finer-grained traces but we should be careful about logging volume. propose sampling at 1% for prod, 100% for canary.
5:30 Sam Rodriguez: also add a synthetic gauge for 'active_kv_entries_per_host' to the dashboard.
5:36 Priya Nair: ok, what's the estimated time to patch staging then canary?
5:42 Omar Habib: patch to staging within 24-36 hours, assuming reviews go smoothly; canary on Tue 2026-04-06 as Sam proposed. full rollout after 48h stable.
5:54 Priya Nair: risks? anything else that could bite us?
5:58 Arjun Singh: host kernel drivers and underlying GPU driver versions — we saw one host with older driver which amplified the kernel timing. need to ensure driver parity on canary hosts.
6:10 Dana Liu: plus we should watch memory fragmentation patterns — not just gross memory. fragmentation can trigger evictions even if free memory looks ok.
6:20 Priya Nair: good catch. Marcus, please add fragmentation checks to stress tests.
6:26 Marcus Yi: will do.
6:28 Tanya Morales: release coordination: if we delay launch by a week, does that block external marketing?
6:34 Lena Ortiz: minimal impact, we'll shift the announcement by one week and coordinate with marketing. better to be safe.
6:40 Priya Nair: ok, let's capture action items — Dana will own RCA and playbook updates, Omar will PR patch, Sam will run canary, Marcus will add tests, Lena will update launch schedule.
6:56 Sam Rodriguez: i want to call out that we need an automated canary harness for these kinds of kernel/kv issues long-term. adding to roadmap: synthetic traffic library + improved canary infra.
7:12 Priya Nair: agree, add it to backlog and we can prioritize in Q2 roadmap.
7:18 Elena Park: one more question: is there any customer data exposure risk?
7:24 Dana Liu: no PII exposure, this was performance only; we did data access audits, nothing abnormal. I'll include confirmation in RCA.
7:30 Priya Nair: ok great. final next steps recap — Dana, Omar, Sam, Marcus, Lena — we have owners and dates, i'll send the meeting notes and RCA link once Dana posts the draft.
7:44 Elena Park: thanks everyone.
7:48 End of recording.
